newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-FERRARA DEDICATES WORLD CLUB WIN TO LOST COUSIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERRARA DEDICATES WORLD CLUB WIN TO LOST COUSIN.

text.p: Juventus defender Ciro Ferrara, who had an outstanding game in his side's 1-0 win over River Plate in the World Club Cup final on Tuesday, dedicated the victory to a young cousin who died earlier this month.

Ferrara, one of seven players in the lineup who helped Juventus win the European Cup Final against Ajax in Rome last May said before catching the plane home that Juventus had so much possesion they could have won by a far bigger scoreline.
"This victory crowns two really intense years," he said, "But 1-0 is a false result, we could have won by far more and now we're going home with our morale sky high.
"I dedicate this win to my cousin Ettore who died 15 days ago. He was barely 32 years old."

Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero added: "It was a tough match because the Argentines moved very well on the ball. Maybe it wasn't a great game but in this kind of final whoever scores first wins. I'm particularly proud because I have never won anything so important before."

Angelo Di Livio, who provided the corner that lead to Alessandro Del Piero's 82nd minute winning goal said: "We played a great team. We could have wrapped the match up earlier but we never managed to cash in on the chances we created. Before Del Piero's winner, we wasted at least five clear scoring chances."

Croatian striker Alen Boksic, who had at least three clear-cut scoring chances -- two in the last five minutes -- admitted: "It's just as well he scored because I missed two chances and things could have got complicated for us if we had gone to extra time.
"Maybe we are not unbeatable but it is hard to find a stronger team than ours. We play every Sunday against dangerous opponents while River Plate often have easy matches.

" I'm particularly happy because three years ago, after winning the European Cup with Marseille, I thought it really unfair that because of the well known events involving president Tapie, Milan played the intercontinental cup even though we had beaten them in the European Cup final."

The match was no classic and was scrappy in parts, but was also very open with both sides prepared to attack. Juventus made more chances than the Argentinian team who came closest to scoring when Ariel Ortego hit the bar with an angled shot after 72 minutes.
